dedupe_keys.name: t drive taxi trajectory data sample beijing

description: The T-Drive trajectory data sample, released by Microsoft Research in August 2011, contains one week of GPS trajectories from 10,357 taxis in Beijing, about 15 million points covering some 9 million kilometres. It comes from the T-Drive project on driving directions learned from taxi drivers' routes, and users are asked to cite two papers, Driving with knowledge from the physical world (KDD 2011) and T-Drive: driving directions based on taxi trajectories (ACM SIGSPATIAL GIS 2010). Coverage is the city of Beijing. Access: free download from the Microsoft Research publication page. Caveats: it is a single week, no licence is stated beyond the citation request, and the Microsoft download centre address in the must-have list now opens the GeoLife data set instead. The data support travel time and route choice estimation for urban road network flow models and benchmark trajectory analysis. They complement the NYC TLC trip records and MobilityDB catalogued here.
